focus: Ponytail runtime portability and rule-copy guards vs sk-code runtime surfaces and drift guards
noveltyJustification: 4 fully new portability/guard mechanisms plus 1 small documentation-staleness finding (invariant list, external-anchor lesson, verified-version rows, generated copies, stale retirement note), 3 already-adopted (delivery prefix stronger, thin adapters, canary discipline).
keyQuestions: How does Ponytail's portability and rule-copy guard surface compare with sk-code's runtime surfaces and drift guards?
answeredQuestions: How does Ponytail's portability and rule-copy guard surface compare with sk-code's runtime surfaces and drift guards?

graphEvents.label: Ponytail portability vs sk-code runtime surfaces

label: Ponytail's copy guard pins ten verbatim rule phrases in both the long-form skill and AGENTS.md, including the never-cut carve-outs (validation at trust boundaries, prevents data loss, security, accessibility) individually, so a reword cannot silently drop one; this is the concrete mechanism for iteration 1's missing local enumeration of never-cut safeguards. Classification: NEW.

sk-code's canary asserts that binding AGENTS.md clauses END inside the smaller runtime truncation prefix (16,384 bytes Devin, 32,768 Codex); Ponytail has no equivalent truncation-position check. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED (stronger).

Ponytail's version guard pins one version across seven files and compares it to the release tag because an agreement test cannot catch uniform staleness (v4.8.0 manifests all stale together while the test passed); cross-file agreement guards in sk-code, including mirror-sync verification, need a truth source outside the pair. Classification: NEW (guard-design lesson).

Ponytail's portability table states support tier and verified host version per adapter row (Verified with Goose 1.53.0, CodeBuddy CLI 2.161.2, Muse Code 1.4.2; Junie marked not automatic yet); sk-code ships surface packets and a manual-testing playbook but no per-surface verified-runtime record. Classification: NEW (portability analogue of confirmed-vs-inferred).

run-all-drift-guards.sh records its retired router-sync check (surface router vs compiled routing snapshot) as missing and does not point at the newer compiled-routing lane, whose activation records name hub-router.json, ROUTER.md and leaf-manifest.json as inputs; the note no longer describes current coverage. Recorded, not resolved. Classification: NEW (small, documentation staleness).

Ponytail's thin-adapter rule (point hosts at existing skills and hooks; only keep copied rule text aligned with AGENTS.md) matches sk-code's consume-don't-copy doctrine, which sk-code enforces with a router-aware alignment verifier and stack-folder verifier run as one gate. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED.

Ponytail generates its transformed OpenClaw skill copies (verbatim bodies, rewritten frontmatter) and fails tests when committed copies are stale, with generation recorded as the canary's upgrade path; sk-code's cross-runtime agent mirrors are hand-maintained, so generation is the stronger mechanism where a copy is pure transformation. Classification: NEW.

Both systems declare the canary-not-generator discipline: sk-code asserts load-bearing substrings and never rewrites; Ponytail documents canary-not-full-equality for the source-of-truth skill comparison. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED.
